Temporal holdouts must be created before fitting the diagnostic backbone. If its checkpoint already learned the held-out interactions, removing targets only from inference histories cannot undo leakage: retrain a separate diagnostic backbone from scratch on the permitted data, or use a checkpoint that never saw those events. Freeze it across history perturbations. Otherwise, describe results as training-history sensitivity, not held-out generalization. This protocol follows the temporal-leakage findings in [Ji et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.11060).

Shared user prefixes are legitimate for predicting existing users’ next interactions; contamination occurs when a held-out event appears as a training label or inside a later training window. Construct windows after splitting, truncate affected histories, and prevent overlapping windows from reintroducing excluded events. For strict temporal claims, use global or rolling cutoffs across all users: per-user truncation still permits future information from other users. Fit popularity statistics and learned preprocessing only on permitted data. Restrict candidates and metadata to availability at prediction time; first observed interaction is only an availability proxy when release dates are unknown. These recommendations synthesize [Time to Split](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748164) and Ji et al.; repeated prefixes also warrant uncertainty estimates clustered by user.

For paired perturbation comparisons, persist each user/cutoff’s target and candidate IDs once, then reuse identical candidates, order, exclusion masks, checkpoint, and tie-breaking. Build exclusions from the original permitted history so deleting an interaction cannot change candidate eligibility. Report paired per-user metric differences. Identical candidates reduce sampling noise but cannot eliminate sampled-ranking bias ([Krichene and Rendle](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651)). Keep these auxiliary diagnostics separate from the unchanged pinned host evaluation: four-category macro HR@10, 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negatives, seed 42.
